correctness.rationale: Unfolding identifies all dual-lattice samples with the complete torus Fourier series of the periodization. After merging equal center-residue/radius classes, each lifted sphere in dimension at least two has a boundary patch avoiding all other locally finite lifted spheres. The nonzero coefficient would give the sole jump there, incompatible with a.e.-zero periodization. For one dimension, the distribution derivative of a periodized interval sum is its signed endpoint measure, and its period integral is total signed length: these are necessary and sufficient for the periodization to vanish. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is a complete linear-independence and alias-kernel theorem for finite weighted Euclidean ball mixtures at one fixed dual lattice, including arbitrary overlaps/radii and a one-dimensional exact converse. Main comparators establish general periodization and anti-aliased connected-set rigidity but do not themselves state these weighted curved-interface consequences. Real searches of both primary literature and the result database found no exact overlap; older curved-boundary reconstruction is a residual publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: Older geometric inverse-problem literature may phrase the curved-boundary independence as a general interface lemma; no universal novelty proof follows from failed search.

value.rationale: A recent published Fourier-lattice sampling classification demonstrates generic aliasing and requires anti-aliasing for its positive rigid theorem. This result gives a natural complete, no-separation inverse classification on finite weighted spherical profiles and a sharp one-dimensional endpoint-flow failure mechanism, across every lattice and all radii. The exact injectivity/kernel statement is independently useful for layered-particle image representations; it is not just a numerical slice or a substitution in a preexisting bound.
